# Dependent-claim malformation specimens
#
# REAL PUBLISHED USPTO CLAIM TEXT, each traceable to its patent and claim
# number. Published claims carry no legal-sensitivity concern, unlike CE's
# generated pseudo-claims, which stay gitignored.
#
# Drawn from two corpora: dep_claims.csv (615 rows, every one containing the
# literal string "of claim" -- a PHRASE FILTER, not a curated malformation set)
# and combined_output_with_allcites_icl_pdpass.csv (99,809 rows, general
# population). Both are untracked and one is 97 MB, so the tests cannot read
# them; these extracted specimens are what the suite runs against.
#
# One block per specimen. PARENT is the claim number a correct implementation
# must resolve, or "-" when the text does not contain one at all. RULE is the
# rule that must be REPORTED -- asserted because the taxonomy is the point: a
# hit resolving the right parent under the wrong rule name cannot tell anyone
# where the next gap is. Rules are tried in order, so RULE also pins that order
# against a later edit silently re-masking a class.
#
# Format:  CLASS / SOURCE / PARENT / TEXT, blocks separated by a blank line.

CLASS   canonical

RULE    canonical

TEXT    4. A solid formed from the method of claim 1.

CLASS   length-catch-all
SOURCE  US8224503 claim 12
RULE    length-catch-all
PARENT  11
TEXT    12. A system according to clam 11, comprising a device for selecting and recording the data, or the signals, or the data and the signals.

# Overlap, recorded rather than hidden: this is a 'clam' misspelling, but
# 'according to clam 1, wherein' also matches the hitachi rule, which is tried
# first. The catch-all is the net for what no NAMED rule sees, so a named rule
# winning here is correct behaviour, not a misfiled specimen.
CLASS   clam-misspelling
SOURCE  US7808305 claim 8
RULE    according-to-hitachi
PARENT  1
TEXT    8. The circuit according to clam 1, wherein each of the first and second elements is a diode.
